source.title: Smooth Inter-layer Propagation of Stabilized Neural Networks for Classification

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports classification accuracy for residual-network variants, but does not measure training classification error or test the stated claim versions. Its discussion of batch normalization and residual-network stability also summarizes cited work.
record.gate_note: The paper's own synthetic-data accuracy results are recorded below as findings about classification performance, not as evidence about training error. UCI and Bitcoin results are test-accuracy results and do not bear on the training-error claim.
record.test_reason: The study measures feature propagation across residual-network layers and classification accuracy, rather than training error, optimization speed, initialization effects, or learning-rate stability thresholds. Its explicit step size h scales the residual forward update; it is not the optimizer learning rate. Comparisons involving batch normalization report accuracy and feature stability, without measuring time to a target accuracy or learning-rate tolerance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the authors conclude that reducing the residual forward-step size smooths feature propagation across layers and often improves accuracy without increasing depth. Batch normalization alone does not always improve accuracy; combining it with a reduced step size can be optimal. They also assert that batch normalization increases training time, but provide no timing comparison or time-to-target-accuracy result.
record.recipe_differences: The study experiments with residual-network step size, shrinkage blocks, and batch normalization on synthetic and non-image datasets; it does not reproduce the claim's training-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: On the synthetic data, reported accuracy changes with step size, shrinkage blocks, batch normalization, and network depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual-update scaling and shrinkage blocks change synthetic-data accuracy and the smoothness of feature propagation across layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual forward-step size and block structure affect feature stability and classification accuracy on the tested synthetic problem.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch normalization alone gives lower synthetic accuracy than vanilla ResNet, while the hybrid with h = 0.1 reaches accuracy 1.0 by layer 250.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization's classification benefit depends on residual forward-step size in this synthetic setting.

record.problems: Synthetic-data findings are presented mainly as visual feature-propagation examples; the text does not identify the reported accuracy as training accuracy. The authors state that batch sizes were not optimized for the UCI experiments.
record.rows_left_out: UCI and Bitcoin results report test accuracy rather than training classification error, so they were not extracted as rows for this claim.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size, regularization, and training-duration conditions.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain convolutional networks and prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Effects of activation-matched, Gaussian, and orthogonal initializations on learning speed and trainable depth.
Optimizer learning rates relative to initial stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on accuracy gained per training time or iteration and optimizer learning-rate tolerance; Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 8 explicitly reports synthetic test accuracy over 10 trials. The layer-visualization passages do not identify their accuracy as training accuracy. The authors' training-time assertion does not establish slower accuracy acquisition under batch normalization, so it warrants no V6 verdict. UCI and Bitcoin test-accuracy results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Training error, CIFAR benchmarks, random or corrupted labels, and the stated model-size and training-duration conditions are not tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or neuron-width comparison.
No plain network without identity shortcuts is compared with the same network using shortcuts; no training-error comparison is reported.
No activation-matched or orthogonal initialization comparison.
Batch normalization is studied, but the reported results do not compare its training speed or learning-rate tolerance on the named benchmark settings.

relation.reason: The paper discusses depth degradation and batch normalization's training benefits, but its own experiments measure different outcomes.

tranche.reason: The reported results concern residual forward-propagation stability and classification accuracy, without testing any claim version's training outcomes. The paper's training-time assertion supplies no matched timing comparison.

source_check.notes: The parameter h scales residual forward updates; layers are not optimizer iterations. The conclusion asserts greater training time with batch normalization, but reports no timing measurements.
